claim: lnxlink (2023.6.0 README on PyPI) is a Linux MQTT companion app for HA that uses MQTT autodiscovery and explicitly supports headless server installation, installed as root with a system service when there is no graphical interface.
stance_target: lnxlink is an adopt candidate for headless Linux fleet machines, with first-class headless install documentation
scope_conditions: lnxlink 2023.6.0 on Debian/Red Hat-based headless Linux; Home Assistant via MQTT
quoted_support: The headless installation is used for linux environments that don't use a Graphical Interface like servers. ... sudo pip3 install -U lnxlink ... When asked, it's recommended to answer false on install as a user service. ... sudo systemctl restart lnxlink.service

claim: lnxlink notifications are one-way: HA publishes JSON to {prefix}/{clientId}/commands/notify with title, message and iconUrl fields; the README documents no action-button response channel or event round-trip to HA.
stance_target: lnxlink cannot deliver actionable notifications without custom extensions
scope_conditions: lnxlink notify module; mqtt.publish from HA
quoted_support: service: mqtt.publish ... topic: {prefix}/{clientId}/commands/notify ... payload: >- { "title": "Notification Title", "message": "Testing notification", "iconUrl": "http://hass.local:8123/local/myimage.jpg" }

claim: lnxlink's control surface includes shutdown, restart, suspend, send keys, bash commands, brightness and boot select, plus monitoring for CPU/RAM/network/idle/battery/disk/updates — but some modules depend on a graphical interface and must be manually removed from the config on headless installs.
stance_target: Headless lnxlink installs require per-host module pruning, adding configuration overhead for fleet adoption
quoted_support: Some modules depend on graphical interface, so if you choose to use this option for installation, you will have to find which ones stop lnxlink from starting and remove them from the config file.
